newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER - PORTUGAL PLAYERS URGE BRIBERY PROBES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - PORTUGAL PLAYERS URGE BRIBERY PROBES.

text.p: The Portuguese soccer players' union on Thursday called for an immediate investigation into a series of scandals and allegations of bribery rocking the domestic game.

The union warned that the incidents, which include accusations of attempted bribery 12 years ago in an European Cup Winners' game involving Porto, were "threatening the image and credibility" of Portuguese soccer.
"The union of professional soccer players...asks that investigations be opened immediately into all these things," it said in a statement.

In the most serious of the allegations, a Portuguese businessman accused Porto soccer club of using him to try to bribe a Romanian referee before an European match against Scotland's Aberdeen in 1984.
Police have already questioned hotel-owner Fernando Barata over the allegations made in a series of interviews with local television, radio and newspapers.
The accusations have been firmly denied by Porto and by the now-retired Romanian referee who had charge of the Aberdeen match.
"I'm totally surprised about these allegations," Ioan Igna told Reuters in Bucharest on Thursday. "I don't know this person who is making accusations. I've never spoken to him."
The players' union said that the government should step in to help draw up new regulations for the running of soccer in Portugal.
